items.title: Inertia group and characters lying above a normal type
items.statement: For N normal in finite G and theta in Irr(N), use the existing left conjugate {}^g theta(n)=theta(g^{-1}ng). Define I=I_G(theta)={g: {}^g theta=theta}, and Irr(H|theta) for N<=H<=G by occurrence in restriction. The action factors through G/N and N<=I<=G.

references.title: Tammo tom Dieck, Representation Theory — §4.2 opening pp.53–54; Späth notation p.1 and §1 opening p.2

items.source_locator: §4.2 opening pp.53–54; Späth notation p.1 and §1 opening p.2
items.proof_plan: Check {}^g({}^h theta)={}^(gh)theta; inner conjugation acts trivially on characters, and stabilizer closure follows from the action. Existing conjugation is reused; only inertia and lying-over terminology are new.

items.title: Translation permutes normal isotypical components
items.statement: For any complex G-module V and N normal in G, g V_theta=V_({}^g theta). Every N-submodule U of V decomposes as the direct sum of U intersect V_theta over the occurring N-types.

references.title: Tammo tom Dieck, Representation Theory — §4.2 pp.53–54 before Proposition 4.2.2; Losev Theorem 2.14(2)
Ivan Losev, Representation Theory, Chapter 0. Basics, Theorem 2.14(2) and Proposition 2.17, pp.10–11

items.proof_plan: The map s -> gs identifies each translated simple submodule with its left conjugate. Apply g and its inverse to the defining isotypical sums. Decompose U by Maschke and place each simple summand into its unique ambient isotypical block. This intersection clause is needed for the converse induction proof.

items.title: Normal restriction has one orbit of constituents
items.statement: For irreducible complex G-module V and any constituent theta of V|N, all constituents form the orbit of theta and all have the same positive multiplicity.

references.title: Tammo tom Dieck, Representation Theory — §4.2 p.54, Proposition 4.2.2 and following formula; Späth Theorem 1.1

items.source_locator: §4.2 p.54, Proposition 4.2.2 and following formula; Späth Theorem 1.1
items.proof_plan: The sum over one orbit is nonzero and G-stable, hence all V. Translation is an isomorphism between components; conjugate simple modules have equal dimensions, so multiplicities agree.

items.title: Clifford restriction formula
items.statement: If chi in Irr(G) lies over theta in Irr(N), I=I_G(theta), then Res_N^G chi=e sum_{gI in G/I} {}^g theta, e a positive integer. Hence chi(1)=e[G:I]theta(1). Use left cosets; the whole restriction need not be isotypical.

references.title: Britta Späth, Reduction theorems for some global-local conjectures — Theorem 1.1 p.2; tom Dieck §4.2 p.54

items.proof_plan: Translate the module decomposition into a character identity and evaluate at 1. The orbit lemma supplies the proof; this theorem supplies the reusable character form.

items.title: Clifford ramification index
items.statement: For chi lying over theta, its ramification index e(chi,theta) is the common multiplicity in the Clifford formula, equivalently dim Hom_N(S,V) for S affording theta.

references.title: Tammo tom Dieck, Representation Theory — §4.2 p.54 after Proposition 4.2.2

items.proof_plan: Positivity and orbit independence come from the formula; Hom dimension is the published multiplicity theorem.

items.title: The stabilizer of a nonzero isotypical component
items.statement: For irreducible V and an occurring theta, the setwise stabilizer of V_theta in G equals I_G(theta). Thus V_theta is an I-module.

references.title: Tammo tom Dieck, Representation Theory — §4.2 p.54 before Proposition 4.2.2

items.proof_plan: Inertia fixes the component by translation. If g fixes it, its nonzero intersection with the conjugate-type component forces equality of types. The occurring/nonzero hypothesis is essential.

items.title: Reconstruction from the inertia component
items.statement: For irreducible V lying over theta, W=V_theta is irreducible over I=I_G(theta), and the canonical G-map Ind_I^G W -> V is an isomorphism.

references.title: Tammo tom Dieck, Representation Theory — Proposition 4.2.2 p.54

items.proof_plan: Use the published covariant-function model: f maps to sum_{t in T} t f(t), T a left transversal. Adjunction verifies equivariance and independence. Each coset block maps bijectively onto tW, and these are the distinct isotypical summands. Establish bijectivity first. For 0<U<W I-stable, the sum of its translates is G-stable with dimension [G:I]dim U strictly between zero and dim V, impossible. No tensor-model identification is assumed.

items.title: Induction of an inertia constituent is irreducible
items.statement: Let I=I_G(theta) and W in Irr(I|theta). Then W|N is theta-isotypical, Ind_I^G W is irreducible, and its theta-isotypical component is the identity-coset copy of W.

references.title: Tammo tom Dieck, Representation Theory — Theorem 4.2.4(1) pp.55–56; Späth Theorem 1.2

items.proof_plan: Apply the orbit lemma within I to get W|N=e theta. The left-coset blocks of the induced function model have distinct N-types {}^t theta; compute the action on each supported block. A nonzero G-submodule meets a block by the intersection lemma. Translate to meet W; I-irreducibility fills W, and G-stability fills all blocks. No invocation of the correspondence itself.

items.title: Clifford correspondence
items.statement: Induction is a bijection Irr(I_G(theta)|theta) -> Irr(G|theta), with inverse taking the theta-isotypical component. Conjugate normal types give the same target set; the sets for distinct G-orbits partition Irr(G).

references.title: Britta Späth, Reduction theorems for some global-local conjectures — Theorem 1.2 p.2; tom Dieck Theorem 4.2.4(1–3,5) pp.55–56

items.source_locator: Theorem 1.2 p.2; tom Dieck Theorem 4.2.4(1–3,5) pp.55–56
items.proof_plan: Reconstruction proves surjectivity. Taking the theta-component after induction recovers W and proves injectivity. The orbit formula gives the disjoint partition. Include I=N and I=G without proper-subgroup assumptions.

items.title: Normal subgroup induction criterion
items.statement: For theta in Irr(N), Ind_N^G theta is irreducible iff I_G(theta)=N. Its character self-inner-product equals [I_G(theta):N].

references.title: Tammo tom Dieck, Representation Theory — Proposition 4.2.3 and equations (4.4)–(4.5) pp.54–55

items.proof_plan: Compute Res_N Ind_N^G as sum {}^t theta over left cosets tN. Reciprocity counts exactly I/N; Schur gives one there and zero elsewhere. Apply the published character criterion.

items.title: Ramification indices account for the inertia quotient
items.statement: For theta in Irr(N), let chi_j run over Irr(G|theta) and e_j=e(chi_j,theta). Then Ind_N^G theta=sum_j e_j chi_j and sum_j e_j^2=[I_G(theta):N].

references.title: Tammo tom Dieck, Representation Theory — Theorem 4.2.4(4), equation (4.7), pp.55–56

items.proof_plan: Reciprocity identifies each induced multiplicity with e_j and excludes other constituents. Take the norm using the published sum-of-squares character identity and the preceding index computation. Retain this cheap source result as a corollary.

items.title: An extension of a normal subgroup representation
items.statement: An extension of S in Irr(N) to H, N<=H<=G, is an H-action on S restricting to the given N-action; at character level Res_N^H chi_tilde=theta. It is automatically irreducible. Inflation from H/N is the published quotient construction.

references.title: Britta Späth, Reduction theorems for some global-local conjectures — Theorem 1.3 p.2; tom Dieck Remark 4.2.5 p.57

items.source_locator: Theorem 1.3 p.2; tom Dieck Remark 4.2.5 p.57
items.proof_plan: Extension keeps the space and N-action. Every H-stable subspace is N-stable, proving irreducibility inline. Invariance is necessary; it does not alone guarantee an extension.

items.title: Isotypical evaluation and multiplicity subspaces
items.statement: If S is irreducible over C and U is a finite theta-isotypical N-module, evaluation S tensor_C Hom_N(S,U) -> U, s tensor f -> f(s), is an N-isomorphism. Every N-submodule is S tensor M0 for a unique multiplicity subspace M0. N-maps between these modules correspond to linear maps between their multiplicity spaces.

references.title: Ivan Losev, Representation Theory, Chapter 0. Basics — §2.3 Theorem 2.14, Corollary 2.16 and Proposition 2.17 pp.10–11

items.proof_plan: Decompose U into copies of S; scalar Schur identifies each Hom coordinate with C. Evaluation becomes the coordinate isomorphism. Apply the same calculation to each submodule using Maschke and its actual inclusion to prove equality of subspaces and uniqueness. Matrices of scalar intertwiners prove the Hom assertion. No density theorem is needed.

items.title: Gallagher correspondence for an extendible type
items.statement: Fix an extension S_tilde of theta to I=I_G(theta). Then eta -> chi_S_tilde Inf_(I/N)^I eta is a bijection Irr(I/N) -> Irr(I|theta). Composing with induction gives Irr(G|theta); the corresponding ramification index is eta(1).

references.title: Britta Späth, Reduction theorems for some global-local conjectures — Theorem 1.3 p.2; tom Dieck Remark 4.2.5 p.57; Losev Corollary 2.16 and Proposition 2.17
Tammo tom Dieck, Representation Theory, Remark 4.2.5, p.57
Ivan Losev, Representation Theory, Chapter 0. Basics, Corollary 2.16 and Proposition 2.17, p.11

items.source_locator: Theorem 1.3 p.2; tom Dieck Remark 4.2.5 p.57; Losev Corollary 2.16 and Proposition 2.17
items.proof_plan: For theta-isotypical I-module U set (i.f)(s)=i f(S_tilde(i)^{-1}s) on Hom_N(S,U). Verify N-linearity, action law and trivial N-action. Evaluation is I-equivariant. By the evaluation lemma N-submodules are S tensor M0, and I-stability is exactly quotient-stability of M0. This proves irreducibility both ways. The Hom clause recovers parameters uniquely; evaluation proves exhaustivity. Multiply characters and compute multiplicity dim M=eta(1).

title: Clifford Theory over Normal Subgroups — Examples

items.title: Clifford correspondence for A3 in S3
items.statement: For A3=<r> in S3, Irr(A3)={1,lambda,lambda^{-1}}, lambda(r)=exp(2 pi i/3). Orbits {1} and {lambda,lambda^{-1}} have inertia S3 and A3. The trivial orbit gives trivial and sign; inducing lambda gives the standard degree-two irrep with ramification one.

references.title: Tammo tom Dieck, Representation Theory — §4.2 Theorem 4.2.4 / Proposition 4.2.3; Späth Theorem 1.3 specialized to S3

items.source_locator: §4.2 Theorem 4.2.4 / Proposition 4.2.3; Späth Theorem 1.3 specialized to S3
items.proof_plan: Compute srs^{-1}=r^{-1}. Realize induction by r=diag(zeta,zeta^{-1}) and s exchanging coordinates; the two r-eigenlines are swapped. Identify these eigenvectors in the coordinate-sum-zero plane of C^3. Verify reducible normal restriction here and mention the published false statement without a load-bearing B-page edge.

items.title: Gallagher correspondence for a direct product
items.statement: For finite N,Q and theta in Irr(N), inertia in N times Q is the full group. Extension S_tilde(n,q)=S(n) yields exactly S external-tensor U, U in Irr(Q), above theta, with ramification dim U.

references.title: Britta Späth, Reduction theorems for some global-local conjectures — Theorem 1.3; tom Dieck Remark 4.2.5 specialized to a direct product

items.source_locator: Theorem 1.3; tom Dieck Remark 4.2.5 specialized to a direct product
items.proof_plan: Check the extension and identify the quotient with Q directly. Apply Gallagher and restrict to dim U copies of S. No prior direct-product classification is needed.

items.title: Boundary normal subgroups in Clifford theory
items.statement: For N=1, theta=1 and I=G; chi restricts to chi(1) copies of 1 and Clifford induction is identity. For N=G, theta=chi, I=G and e=1; the lying-over correspondence is the singleton identity.

references.title: Britta Späth, Reduction theorems for some global-local conjectures — Theorems 1.1–1.3; tom Dieck Theorem 4.2.4 boundary specializations

items.source_locator: Theorems 1.1–1.3; tom Dieck Theorem 4.2.4 boundary specializations
items.proof_plan: Substitute each extreme in the definitions. At N=1 the trivial extension recovers Irr(G) by Gallagher; at N=G the quotient is trivial. Distinguish homogeneous from irreducible restriction.
